Plan: the cavity is a plain rectangular box, so a single graded-free `blockMesh` block is the right mesher — hex cells, all six faces in one `walls` patch, and the two 20 mm cubes become `cellZone`s via `topoSet` box sources. Cell size is chosen so the zone faces land exactly on cell faces. First cell: build the box and the two marker cubes in build123d, measure them, and look at them.

```python
from build123d import *
import numpy as np, os

# ---- parameters (metres) ----
LX, LY, LZ = 0.100, 0.060, 0.040      # cavity 100 x 60 x 40 mm
CUBE = 0.020                          # 20 mm marker cubes
GAP_Z = 0.005                         # gap from floor / ceiling
GAP_X = 0.010                         # gap from the end walls

cavity = Box(LX, LY, LZ).moved(Location((LX/2, LY/2, LZ/2)))   # corner at origin

heater = Box(CUBE, CUBE, CUBE).moved(Location((GAP_X + CUBE/2, LY/2, GAP_Z + CUBE/2)))
cooler = Box(CUBE, CUBE, CUBE).moved(Location((LX - GAP_X - CUBE/2, LY/2, LZ - GAP_Z - CUBE/2)))

for nm, s in [("cavity", cavity), ("heater", heater), ("cooler", cooler)]:
    bb = s.bounding_box()
    print(f"{nm:7s} bbox min={np.round(bb.min.to_tuple(),4)} max={np.round(bb.max.to_tuple(),4)} "
          f"size={np.round((bb.max - bb.min).to_tuple(),4)} vol={s.volume:.3e} m^3")
print("cubes inside cavity:", (cavity & heater).volume/heater.volume, (cavity & cooler).volume/cooler.volume)
```

Dimensions are exactly as asked. Now look at the arrangement — cavity outline with the two cubes inside, to confirm heater sits low at the x=0 end and cooler high at the x=L end.

```python
import pyvista as pv
pv.start_xvfb() if hasattr(pv, "start_xvfb") else None
pl = pv.Plotter(off_screen=True, window_size=(900, 650))
pl.add_mesh(pv.Box(bounds=(0, LX, 0, LY, 0, LZ)), style="wireframe", color="k", line_width=2)
pl.add_mesh(pv.Box(bounds=(0.01, 0.03, 0.02, 0.04, 0.005, 0.025)), color="red", opacity=0.8)
pl.add_mesh(pv.Box(bounds=(0.07, 0.09, 0.02, 0.04, 0.015, 0.035)), color="blue", opacity=0.8)
pl.add_axes()
pl.camera_position = [(0.25, -0.22, 0.16), (0.05, 0.03, 0.02), (0, 0, 1)]
pl.screenshot("layout.png")
print("red=heater (low, x~0.02)  blue=cooler (high, x~0.08)")
```

Now the two cell zones via `topoSet` box sources (boxes coincide with cell faces, so cell centres fall unambiguously inside).

```python
import subprocess, textwrap

def zone_entries(name, bmin, bmax):
    return textwrap.dedent(f"""\
    {{ name {name}Set; type cellSet; action new; source boxToCell;
      box ({bmin[0]} {bmin[1]} {bmin[2]}) ({bmax[0]} {bmax[1]} {bmax[2]}); }}
    {{ name {name}; type cellZoneSet; action new; source setToCellZone; set {name}Set; }}
    """)

H = ((0.010, 0.020, 0.005), (0.030, 0.040, 0.025))
C = ((0.070, 0.020, 0.015), (0.090, 0.040, 0.035))

open("system/topoSetDict","w").write(
    "FoamFile { version 2.0; format ascii; class dictionary; object topoSetDict; }\n"
    "actions (\n" + zone_entries("heater", *H) + zone_entries("cooler", *C) + ");\n")

r = subprocess.run(["topoSet"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(r.returncode, r.stdout[-1200:], r.stderr[-500:])
```

Zones are 64 cells each = 8.0e-6 m³, matching the 20 mm cubes exactly. Shape confirmed at the coarse level; now refine to 2.5 mm cells (40×24×16 = 15360), which still aligns every zone face, and re-run topoSet.

```python
import subprocess, textwrap

CELL_FINE = 0.0025
nx, ny, nz = round(LX/CELL_FINE), round(LY/CELL_FINE), round(LZ/CELL_FINE)
d = open("system/blockMeshDict").read()
d = d.replace(f"({20} {12} {8})", f"({nx} {ny} {nz})")
open("system/blockMeshDict","w").write(d)

print(subprocess.run(["blockMesh"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout[-500:])
print(subprocess.run(["topoSet"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout[-450:])
```

checkMesh, then dump each cellZone to VTK so I can measure its actual bounds and see it in place.

```python
import subprocess
cm = subprocess.run(["checkMesh"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
print(cm[cm.find("Checking geometry"):][:1500])
for z in ("heater","cooler"):
    r = subprocess.run(["foamToVTK","-cellZone",z,"-time","0","-overwrite"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(z, r.returncode, r.stdout[-120:])
```

checkMesh printed nothing useful from my slice, and foamToVTK exited 1. Look at both in full.

```python
import subprocess
r = subprocess.run(["checkMesh"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(r.returncode); print(r.stdout[-2000:])
r2 = subprocess.run(["foamToVTK","-cellZone","heater","-overwrite"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print("foamToVTK:", r2.returncode, r2.stdout[-400:], r2.stderr[-400:])
```

Mesh OK, and checkMesh itself reports both zone bounding boxes exactly at the requested cubes. Final look: export each zone to VTK and render it inside the mesh outline.

```python
import subprocess, glob, pyvista as pv
from IPython.display import Image, display

for z in ("heater","cooler"):
    subprocess.run(["foamToVTK","-cellZone",z,"-overwrite","-name",f"VTK_{z}"], capture_output=True, text=True)
files = {z: sorted(glob.glob(f"VTK_{z}/**/*.vtk", recursive=True) + glob.glob(f"VTK_{z}/**/*.vtu", recursive=True)) for z in ("heater","cooler")}
print(files)

pl = pv.Plotter(off_screen=True, window_size=(900,650))
pl.add_mesh(pv.Box(bounds=(0,LX,0,LY,0,LZ)), style="wireframe", color="k")
for z, col in (("heater","red"), ("cooler","blue")):
    m = pv.read(files[z][0]); print(z, m.n_cells, m.bounds)
    pl.add_mesh(m, color=col, show_edges=True)
pl.add_axes(); pl.camera_position = [(0.25,-0.22,0.16),(0.05,0.03,0.02),(0,0,1)]
pl.screenshot("zones.png"); display(Image("zones.png"))
```

Built and meshed a sealed rectangular air cavity with two marked cell zones.

**Geometry (metres, built directly in SI — no scaling involved).** Box with corner at the origin, 0.100 × 0.060 × 0.040 m; z is vertical, so gravity would act along −z. Measured from the build123d solid and again from the mesh: bounding box (0 0 0)–(0.1 0.06 0.04), total volume 2.400e-04 m³ = 0.1·0.06·0.04 exactly.

**Mesh.** Single `blockMesh` block, 40 × 24 × 16 = 15360 uniform hexes at 2.5 mm. checkMesh: *Mesh OK* — max non-orthogonality 0, max skewness 3.3e-14, aspect ratio 1, all cell volumes 1.5625e-08 m³. I built and inspected it first at 5 mm / 1920 cells, then refined; the 2.5 mm size was chosen so every zone face lands on a cell face (no partial cells in either zone).

**Boundaries.** One patch, `walls`, of type `wall`, containing all six faces, defined face-by-face in the blockMeshDict (floor, ceiling, y=0, y=LY, x=0, x=LX — named at the point of definition, not by bounding-box lookup). No inlet, no outlet; checkMesh reports the patch closed and singly connected, 3968 faces. It is up to the solver setup to give it a zero-gradient (adiabatic) thermal condition — I set no boundary conditions, per the scope of this desk.

**Cell zones.** `heater`: 512 cells, volume 8.0e-06 m³, bbox (0.01 0.02 0.005)–(0.03 0.04 0.025) — a 20 mm cube, 5 mm above the floor, 10 mm from the x=0 end wall, centred in y. `cooler`: 512 cells, volume 8.0e-06 m³, bbox (0.07 0.02 0.015)–(0.09 0.04 0.035) — matching 20 mm cube, 5 mm below the ceiling, 10 mm from the x=0.1 end wall. Both confirmed independently by checkMesh's cellZone table and by re-reading the exported zone VTKs.

**Not checked / decisions I made.** The request did not specify where in the cavity the cubes sit, so I chose 5 mm stand-off from floor/ceiling and 10 mm from the end walls, centred in y; change those four constants at the top of the cell if you wanted them touching the walls instead. The six walls share one patch name rather than being split into floor/ceiling/sides — say the word if you need them separately for per-face conditions. The `VTK_heater` / `VTK_cooler` directories are visualisation byproducts and can be deleted.
